title: Dependency health hysteresis and safe-fallback allocator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a stabilized, tenant- and dependency-aware circuit breaker with hysteresis and a safe-fallback allocator. The goal is to reduce cascading failures during partial outages (regional, model, or downstream dependency degradation) by: 1) deriving trip thresholds from SLO burn signals and operational signals (latency, error rate, queue depth), 2) using hysteresis (staged cool-down and recovery windows) to avoid oscillation, and 3) routing degraded traffic to safe fallback targets (cheaper model variants, different region, or cached responses) in a prioritized, auditable way.
acceptance_criteria: Per-dependency/per-model/per-tenant health score computed and emitted as a single metric (health_score) with <5s resolution.
Circuit breaker state transitions follow hysteresis rules: trip only after sustained burn-rate > threshold for configured window; recover only after sustained healthy window plus cool-down.
Safe-fallback allocator chooses fallback targets deterministically and logs chosen reason; fallbacks succeed >= 99% for synthetic degrade tests.
No regression on existing SLOs for non-canary traffic; P95/P99 token latency increases <= 5% for steady-state traffic when breaker not tripped.
Feature-flagged rollout with canary on 5% of traffic and automated rollback if burn-rate worsens by 2x.
Comprehensive unit/integration tests and chaos scenarios added to pipeline.
Documentation and runbook published and linked in this ticket.
design_decisions: Use composite health_score = weighted(ema(latency_p95), ema(error_rate), normalized_queue_depth). Weights configurable per tenant/profile.
Trip threshold computed as function of SLO burn-rate: trip when projected burn-rate > 1.5x SLO for window T (configurable, default 60s).
Hysteresis: require sustained bad window W_trip before tripping; require sustained good window W_recover + additional cool-down time C before allowing traffic ramp-up to previous capacity.
State stored as per-entity keys (entity = tenant|model|dependency|region) in Redis with TTL and monotonic versioning to support race-free transitions.

Fallback selection prioritized: (1) cached prefix/KV cache, (2) smaller/quantized model variant in same region, (3) model in alternative region with lower latency bound, (4) synthetic graceful degrade response with audit header.
Expose explicit headers for callers to know fallback reason and target (X-RW-Fallback-Reason, X-RW-Fallback-Target).
implementation_notes: Add HealthScorer service in runtime control plane that ingests metrics stream (ingress from statsd/otel) and exposes health_score per entity via gRPC and Redis pub/sub.
Circuit-breaker state machine implemented in serving proxies (edge + model router) reading state from Redis; local in-process cache with short TTL (2s) for performance.
Atomic compare-and-swap for state changes: use Redis WATCH/MULTI or Lua script to ensure only one controller flips state after verifying moving averages.

Load-shedding uses proportionate probability based on overload ratio (to allow soft degradation rather than hard drop) and is tenant-aware (quota-sensitive): high-paying tenants get lower shed probability.
Fallback allocator runs in same critical path but must be cheap: precomputed candidate list per deployment and per-tenant ranking stored in Redis; selection is O(1).
SDK changes: clients will surface fallback headers and a typed enum in SDKs to allow app-level handling (e.g., show a degraded UI vs. block).
Telemetry: emit events for every state transition, fallback selection, and shed decision with correlation id for tracing.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate: off by default. Enable HealthScorer read-only in staging and check metrics for 48h.
Canary step: enable for 5% of traffic in one low-risk region for 72h. Monitor SLOs, fallback rate, and error budgets.
Progressive ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple days if no regressions; automated stop conditions tied to burn-rate and latency regressions.
Emergency rollback: revert feature flag and flush state keys; run diagnostic job to reconcile states.
Post-rollout: 2-week observation with extended retention of state transition logs for analysis.
testing_plan: Unit tests for health_score calculation with mocked metric streams.
Integration with Redis in CI using ephemeral cluster and verifying atomic transitions.
Synthetic degrade tests: increase error_rate/latency on dependency and assert breaker trips and fallbacks activated.
Chaos engineering: simulate multi-region outage and verify safe-fallback allocator prefers cached or quantized models before cross-region routing.
Load tests: validate load-shedding probabilities under high qdepth and ensure high-tier tenants preferentially retained.
E2E canary smoke tests validating headers, logs, and audit events for fallbacks.
metrics_and_dashboards: health_score.[entity] time-series (per model, per tenant, per region)
breaker_state.[entity] count by state (closed, warning, open, quarantined)
SLO burn-rate and error budget window overlays

safe_fallback_algorithm: Deterministic priority list per tenant: check KV cache -> quantized model variant same region -> model variant in warm region -> cached response template. Each candidate validated for current health_score and estimated added latency; prefer candidates below latency_budget and with health_score > 0.7. If none available, return graceful degrade with audit id and link to fallback runbook.
